findings.message: The ban on looking up the story's own estimate is stated three times (intro, first bullet of 'What not to read', and the ID-search bullet).
findings.detail: "the other card exists but you must not look for it"; "Never look for an estimate of the story you are estimating or of its tasks, wherever it is"; "Do not search the repo for the story's ID or its tasks' IDs." The last is a concrete means of the second, so it adds a little, but the intro line is a pure restatement. Consolidated wording: keep the 'What not to read' rule ("Never look for an estimate of this story or its tasks, and do not search the repo for their IDs") and shorten the intro to "you estimate alone and blind".

findings.message: The ban on design and implementation questions is stated three times (What to read, Format, Guidelines).
findings.detail: Quotes: "they pull you towards design questions, which belong to the OpenSpec change, not to the story" (What to read); "phrased as a concrete question or situation, not as a solution" (Format); "Do not ask about implementation (types, formats, protocols, internal contracts): that is the spec's job" (Guidelines). Consolidated wording: keep the single rule in Guidelines ("Do not ask about implementation or propose solutions: design belongs to the OpenSpec change") and shorten the other two to the reading restriction only.

findings.message: "Use it sparingly" for the `spec` tag gives no limit or criterion for when it is allowed.
findings.detail: "`spec`: a design question for the OpenSpec change. Use it sparingly." Readings: at most one of the 3 out-of-criteria notes, or only when no other tag fits. The guidelines already ban implementation questions, so behaviour barely changes. Rewrite: "`spec`: a design question for the OpenSpec change. At most one per review, and only when none of the other tags fits."

findings.message: The quota guidance restates the same point three ways in two sentences (about 15 words could be saved).
findings.detail: "Return fewer if you find fewer: there is no quota. Five solid ones beat eight padded ones." Tightened: "Return fewer if you find fewer; there is no quota."

findings.message: "short log excerpts (a few lines, not whole logs)" gives no line count for how much log to copy into the evidence.
findings.detail: "short log excerpts (a few lines, not whole logs)". Readings range from 3 to 30 lines, which changes how much text reaches the capture. Rewrite: "log excerpts of at most 10 lines around the error." Only the author can fix the exact number.

findings.message: The rule that the capturer must not decide classification fields is stated twice (intro and 'Nothing else' list).
findings.detail: "You do not decide anything that classifying decides (type, epic, priority, duplicates): you only suggest." and "Nothing else: no `labels`, `priority`, `parentId`, `estimate` or `assignee`. They are set when classifying...". Consolidate: keep the intro statement and have the Writing section only list the permitted fields, noting that everything else is left for classifying.

findings.message: The 'title is not an action / no infinitive verb' rule is restated within the Title paragraph (3 phrasings).
findings.detail: "not an action", "An action already presumes a type...", "So the title never starts with a verb in the infinitive". Consolidate: "The title names the need or what was seen, never an action (no leading infinitive verb, since an action presumes a type); e.g. 'Nivel de audio en grande en el panel'."

findings.message: The title directive asks for a "short" title without a length limit.
findings.detail: Quote: "**Title.** Short, in Spanish, naming the need or what was seen". Readings: 5 words, 10 words, or one line; the result barely changes behaviour. Proposed rewrite: "Title: at most 10 words, in Spanish, naming the need or what was seen."

findings.message: The goal "write it down faithfully and fast" gives no acceptance criterion for "fast".
findings.detail: Quote: "Your job is to write it down faithfully and fast". Readings: minimal tool calls, or no extra reasoning; the rest of the document (one save_issue call, no other tools) already narrows it. Proposed rewrite: "Create the capture with a single save_issue call and no other Linear calls."

findings.message: That the user decides and approves the verdict before anything is written is stated twice (intro and step 2).
findings.detail: "**The decision is the user's**: you draft, they decide." and "The user corrects or rewrites it. Do not move on until they approve it, because every later step writes it down." Consolidate: keep step 2's gating rule and trim the intro to "you draft the verdict; the user approves it (step 2)."

findings.message: The directive on uncommitted changes says to ask whether they belong to the experiment but not what to do for each answer.
findings.detail: "If there are uncommitted changes, ask whether they belong to the experiment before going on." If the user says yes, the skill does not say whether to commit them first; if no, it does not say whether to stash, leave, or stop. Suggested rewrite: "If there are uncommitted changes, ask whether they belong to the experiment: if yes, commit them with `Refs MOO-n` before continuing; if no, stop and ask the user to set them aside."

findings.message: The rule that nothing is written to Linear before the user validates is stated twice (intro and step 3).
findings.detail: Quotes: "the user validates every story before anything is written to Linear" (intro) and "Nothing goes to Linear without explicit approval" (step 3). Consolidated wording: keep the rule only in step 3 (Human gate) and drop the clause from the Input paragraph.

findings.message: "Read the parts you need" of the source document does not say which parts count as needed.
findings.detail: "Read the parts you need through that table... the epic's story or stories..., its expectations, scope, users, open questions and glossary." The list that follows mostly resolves it, so the ambiguity rarely changes behaviour. Tighten: "Read the epic's stories, expectations, scope, users, open questions and glossary through that table."

findings.message: The description hides that the skill writes to Linear (updates the story and creates task sub-issues) and that Spike-labelled issues are refused.
findings.detail: Current description: "Refine a Mood Table user story that is in Backlog in Linear. ... adds the DoD by type, technical context and the proposed tasks." Body evidence: step 12 calls `save_issue` to update the story and create each approved task as a sub-issue; step 1 stops for issues labelled `Spike`. It does cue the moment (story in Backlog, second step of the flow), so the mismatch is minor. Suggested: "Refine a Mood Table user story in Backlog in Linear (not a Spike): the user writes the happy path, the AI translates it to GIVEN/WHEN/THEN, the poke-holes subagent finds gaps and the user keeps 3-5; checks INVEST (stops to propose a split if it fails), adds the DoD by type and technical context, and after approval saves the story and creates its task sub-issues. Use after /create-story and before /estimate-story."

findings.message: "If it fails two or more" INVEST criteria does not say whether a ⚠️ counts as a failure or only ❌ does.
findings.detail: Steps 3 and 9 grade each criterion ✅/⚠️/❌, then say "If it fails **two or more**, the story is not ready". Reading A: only ❌ counts; reading B: ⚠️ and ❌ both count. They lead to different actions (split vs. continue). Rewrite: "If two or more criteria are ❌, the story is not ready: propose how to split it..." (or state that ⚠️ counts too).

findings.message: "show it briefly and carry on" leaves the length of the passing INVEST summary unspecified.
findings.detail: "If it passes, show it briefly and carry on; the full check comes back in step 9." Candidate readings: the six one-line results, or just a one-line verdict. Rewrite: "If it passes, show the six one-line results and carry on."

findings.message: Step 5 explains twice why the subagent must not see the GWT translation; about two sentences could be cut.
findings.detail: Quote: "The value of the subagent is that it has not seen what was already decided, so it does not share the author's blind spots. Your translation is already an interpretation, with its (asumido) gaps filled in your way; passing it would hand the subagent your blind spots too." Tightened wording: "Never pass your GWT translation: it carries your (asumido) gaps and would hand the subagent your blind spots."

findings.message: The 'grey areas or risks' trigger for stopping gives no test for when a decision qualifies.
findings.detail: "When a decision has grey areas or risks, stop and say so, with reasoning and alternatives." Two agents could disagree on whether a decision is grey, so the stop rule fires inconsistently. Suggested rewrite: "Stop and say so when a decision is not covered by the PRD, README or D# decisions, or when it is hard to reverse (schema, public API, hardware wiring); give reasoning and at least two alternatives."

findings.message: 'Complete before extensive' gives no criterion for when a flow counts as complete.
findings.detail: "Complete before extensive: one closed, excellent flow beats broad coverage." It does not say what makes a flow closed or excellent, so an agent cannot decide when to stop polishing one flow and start another. Suggested rewrite: "Finish one flow end to end (its acceptance criteria met, tests green, DoD checked) before starting another."

findings.message: That `readme.md` and `prompts.md` are mandatory is stated twice in §3 (the template line and the closing bullet of the delivery mechanics).
findings.detail: "**Plantilla oficial:** un `readme.md` con 8 secciones + `prompts.md`." and "`readme.md` y `prompts.md`, obligatorios siempre." Consolidated wording: keep only the template line and add "(ambos obligatorios en cada entrega)".

findings.message: The extension request says to ask the TA "con antelación" without giving a lead time.
findings.detail: Quote: "Prórroga posible hasta el 25-nov, pidiéndola al TA con antelación". Readings: days before the delivery date, or before the deadline passes. Only the author or LIDR can fix the number. Proposed rewrite: "pidiéndola al TA al menos N días antes de la fecha de entrega (N a confirmar con el TA)".

findings.message: The tip "iterar el PRD hasta que lo cubra todo" has no acceptance criterion for "todo".
findings.detail: Quote: "iterar el PRD hasta que lo cubra todo". Readings: every story and expectation of the idea, every evaluation axis, or every section of the official template. Proposed rewrite: "iterar el PRD hasta que cada historia tenga expectativas, alcance y glosario, y cada decisión dé juego en los tres ejes (§2)".

findings.message: The GitHub-driven state transitions (draft PR, open PR, merged PR) are listed in the §2 state table and again in the §7 automations bullet (two statements).
findings.detail: §2: "In Progress | Implementándose (PR en borrador) | GitHub (automático)", "In Review | PR abierta...", "Done | PR integrada". §7: "Automatizaciones: PR en borrador → `In Progress` · PR abierta → `In Review` · revisión pedida → `In Review` · PR integrada → `Done`." Only 'revisión pedida → In Review' is new. Consolidated wording: in §7 keep just "Automatizaciones: las de la tabla de estados (§2), más revisión pedida → `In Review`."

findings.message: The directive to review the permission list when Linear publishes new tools names no trigger, owner or check.
findings.detail: Quote: "Las herramientas nuevas que publique Linear no quedan cubiertas: caen en el modo de permisos por defecto. Hay que revisar la lista si aparece alguna." Readings: review on every Linear MCP update, or only when someone notices a new tool; and which list (the allow/ask/deny entries in .claude/settings.json). Proposed rewrite: "Cuando `mcp__linear__*` exponga una herramienta que no esté en `allow` ni en `deny` de `.claude/settings.json`, el mantenedor la añade a `allow`, `ask` o `deny` en la misma PR que la use."

findings.message: That a panel ignores a message type it does not know is stated three times (type 5 notes, type 7 notes, and the closing section).
findings.detail: "Un panel que no conoce el tipo `5` lo ignora."; "Un panel que no conoce el tipo `7` lo ignora."; "Lo ignora, también si es de un tipo que todavía no conoce." The closing section already covers every type, present and future. Consolidated wording: drop the two per-type sentences and keep only the closing rule, "Un panel ignora cualquier mensaje que no entiende, también el de un tipo que todavía no conoce."

findings.message: The rule "one task = one PR, one step = one commit" is restated in the chain table, in §2 and again in §5 (3 times).
findings.detail: §1: "una tarea = una PR" / "cada paso = un commit"; §2 title "Granularidad: tarea → PR, paso → commit" and its table; §5: "Tarea → PR, paso → commit: no mezclar dos tareas en una PR ni dos pasos en un commit." Keep §2 as the single statement and reduce §5 to a pointer: "Tarea → PR, paso → commit (§2); un spike es una PR con commits libres (§7)."

findings.message: "Write each datum in one place and link elsewhere" appears in §3 and again in §5 ("No duplicar").
findings.detail: §3: "Cada dato se escribe en **un solo sitio**; en los demás, se enlaza." and §5: "**No duplicar:** si algo ya está en otro sitio de la tabla del §3, enlázalo." Consolidate by keeping §3 and dropping the §5 bullet, or making it a bare cross-reference.
